-- The expectation-merging corpus. One input per line; a blank line or a line
-- starting with a double dash is skipped.
--
-- The grammar the harness runs over these is deliberately alternative-shaped:
-- at operand position it tries a parenthesized group, then a bracketed group,
-- then a bare atom, restoring the cursor between attempts. So each of these
-- inputs sends at least one alternative some distance into the stream before it
-- fails and the parse rewinds, which is exactly the situation where a refusal
-- gets reported at the wrong position.
--
-- One alternative goes deep and later ones fail immediately: the report must
-- name the deep position and only the expectation recorded there.
[1 + 2
(1 + 2
1 + [2
[1 + 2)
(1 + 2]
-- Every alternative fails at the same position: the report must name all of
-- them, in the order they were tried.
*
1 +
-
[)
-- The driver declines a repeated non-associative operator, and the leftover
-- operator is refused where it stands.
1 == 2 == 3
1 2
-- Accepted, for contrast.
1 + 2 * (3 - 4)
[1 + 2] ?? -3
